html:
The Khmelnytsky Uprising was a Cossack and peasant revolt against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in Ukraine, led by Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky from 1648 until his death in 1657.

Allied with the Crimean Tatars, the Zaporozhian Cossacks won great victories in 1648 and set up a Cossack state, the Hetmanate, with its capital at Chyhyryn. Rebels massacred Polish nobles, Catholic priests and many thousands of Jews, a catastrophe in Jewish memory. In 1654 at Pereiaslav, Khmelnytsky accepted the protection of the Russian tsar, which led to war between Russia and Poland and the division of Ukraine along the Dnieper. Ukrainians see him as a founder of their state; Russians long saw Pereiaslav as a reunion. It helped bring on the Deluge that ruined the Commonwealth.
sum: The Khmelnytsky Uprising was a Cossack and peasant revolt against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in Ukraine, led by Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky from 1648 until his death in 1657.
